passage:
"Rehana, why are you standing behind the others?"
"No reason, Sir."
"You've got your bag on your shoulder in PE again."
Rehana tugged her hair over her face. "I just grew so much this year. I feel like a lamppost."
Jagdish Sir nodded slowly. "Growing fast feels strange. Everyone's body changes at a different speed. Nothing's wrong with yours."
"Everyone looks at me."
"Maybe. Can I show you something?" He tossed her the netball. "Try a shot from here."
She sighed, dropped the bag, and threw. It went in.
"Again."
It went in again. Two girls from the back cheered.
"Your long arms are brilliant for this, you know. Come to practice Thursday?"
Rehana pushed her hair back and grinned. "Maybe. Okay. Yes."

qa.q: What did Jagdish Sir toss to Rehana?
qa.a: He tossed her the netball.

qa.q: How did Rehana feel about her body at the start?
qa.a: She felt awkward and self-conscious, like a lamppost, which is why she stood behind the others and hid behind her hair and bag.

qa.q: How did Jagdish Sir help Rehana, and why did it work?
qa.a: He calmly reassured her that bodies change at different speeds, then let her enjoy a shot, so she felt capable instead of watched.

qa.q: How might the two girls who cheered see Rehana now?
qa.a: They see a teammate who can shoot well, not someone too tall, which may help her feel she belongs.

grounding: It shows a teenager who feels awkward about a growing body and hides behind a bag and hair, until kind reassurance and enjoyable movement help.

passage:
Last year I lived inside my brother's old grey hoodie, even in April. I'd grown in ways that felt too sudden, and my skin broke out. I walked with my shoulders rounded and my hair over my face, like I could fold myself smaller.
Nazia noticed. She didn't say anything about how I looked. She just said, "There's a free dance class at the community hall on Saturday. Come with me, I don't want to go alone."
The first ten minutes I stood at the back, arms crossed. Then the teacher put on an old film song and everyone was laughing and getting the steps wrong. I forgot about my hoodie. I spun around and almost hit Nazia.
Walking home, I realised my shoulders weren't hunched. I felt like me.

Pooja

qa.q: Where was the free dance class?
qa.a: It was at the community hall.

qa.q: How did Pooja feel at the start of the dance class?
qa.a: Pooja felt shy and self-conscious, standing at the back with arms crossed.

qa.q: What did Nazia do that helped?
qa.a: Nazia didn't comment on Pooja's looks and simply invited Pooja to something fun, so Pooja could enjoy moving instead of hiding.

qa.q: Why might Nazia have said she didn't want to go alone?
qa.a: Nazia may have wanted to make it easy for Pooja to say yes, turning the invitation into a favour between friends instead of advice.

grounding: It shows a teenager uneasy about a changing body who slumps and hides under a hoodie and hair, and who feels at home again by enjoying a dance class.

passage:
'Ojas, beta, why are you walking like a question mark?'
'I'm not.'
Rashmi Maasi raised an eyebrow. Ojas had grown nearly a hand's width since summer, and now he hunched everywhere, backpack clutched to his chest.
'Everyone keeps saying how tall I've got. I feel like a giraffe. My arms don't fit anywhere.'
'Ah. The awkward growing year. I had it at thirteen too. I used to hide behind my hair.'
'Did it stop?'
'It did. You'll grow into yourself.' She paused. 'Want to play badminton with me on Sunday? Tall people are amazing at the net.'
Ojas almost smiled. 'I'll probably trip.'
'Then we'll trip together.'
On Sunday he did trip, twice. He also smashed a shot past her and whooped, standing straight up without thinking.

qa.q: What was Ojas clutching to his chest?
qa.a: His backpack.

qa.q: How was Ojas feeling about his growing body?
qa.a: He felt awkward and self-conscious, like a giraffe whose arms did not fit anywhere.

qa.q: What helped Ojas start to feel at home in his body?
qa.a: Rashmi Maasi's kind reassurance and inviting him to enjoy badminton, where his height was an advantage.

qa.q: How might Rashmi Maasi have felt watching him whoop on Sunday?
qa.a: She was probably pleased and warm, seeing him forget to hunch for a moment.

grounding: Shows a teenager slumping and hiding behind a bag because he feels awkward about a growing body, and kind reassurance and enjoyable movement helping.

passage: The year I was thirteen, my body felt like it belonged to someone else. My voice cracked in the middle of sentences. My arms and legs suddenly seemed too long, and I kept knocking things over. So I shrank. I wore my brother's huge hoodie every day, hunched in the back row, and hid behind my bag at the bus stop. I'm Tarun, and I thought if I stayed small enough, nobody would notice. My friend Lakshmi noticed. 'You used to be the best dancer at every wedding,' she said. 'Come to the Saturday class with me.' I said no four times. The fifth time I went. Nobody laughed. The teacher said, 'Long arms, beautiful lines.' I left sweaty and grinning, standing up straight for the first time in months.

qa.q: What did Tarun wear every day?
qa.a: A brother's huge hoodie.

qa.q: How did Tarun feel about that changing body at thirteen?
qa.a: Tarun felt awkward and embarrassed, as if the body belonged to someone else.

qa.q: What helped Tarun feel more at home?
qa.a: Lakshmi's kind invitation and enjoying dance again, where the teacher praised the long arms.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi have felt when Tarun finally came to class?
qa.a: Lakshmi was probably pleased and relieved, after asking five times.

grounding: Shows a teenager hiding behind clothes and a bag because of an awkward growing body, and kind reassurance and enjoyment of movement helping.

passage:
PE teacher's note, Class 8
Since the new term, Sumit has been hiding behind his bag and slumping at the back of every line. He no longer wants to change for PE and pulls his sleeves over his hands. He has grown a lot this year and I think he feels awkward and watched. I didn't mention it in front of the class. After school I asked him privately whether PE felt uncomfortable lately. He shrugged, red-faced, and said everyone looks at him because he's grown so much. I told him that growing bodies are awkward for a while and he wasn't doing anything wrong. I asked if he'd lead the warm-up stretches, since he's tall enough for everyone to see. He did it today, a bit shy, then enjoyed it. He stood up straight for the whole session.
Sarika

qa.q: What does Sumit pull over his hands?
qa.a: His sleeves.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling during PE lately?
qa.a: He felt awkward and self-conscious, as if everyone was looking at his growing body.

qa.q: What did Sarika do that helped Sumit?
qa.a: Sarika spoke privately and kindly, reassured him, and gave him a role leading warm-ups so he could enjoy moving.

qa.q: How might the rest of the class see Sumit leading warm-ups?
qa.a: They probably saw a confident, tall classmate, not the awkward boy he feared they saw.

grounding: Shows a teenager slumping and hiding because of a growing body, and a teacher's private reassurance and enjoyable movement helping him feel at home in himself.

passage:
Tuesday
Grew again. Uniform pants are above my ankles and everyone in 9B noticed. I've started walking with my bag held in front of me and my shoulders pulled in, like that'll make me shorter. In assembly I stood at the very back and slouched so hard my back hurt. Yamini didi saw me at the bus stop and said, "Why are you walking like a question mark?" I wanted to disappear. But on the way home she didn't tease. She said she also hated her height in school until she joined the volleyball team, and now her long arms "are a weapon". She's taking me to evening practice at the ground on Saturday. I'm scared I'll trip over my own feet. Still, I said yes.
Tanvir

qa.q: What did Yamini didi say at the bus stop?
qa.a: She said, "Why are you walking like a question mark?"

qa.q: How does Tanvir feel about the growth spurt, and what shows it?
qa.a: Tanvir feels awkward and self-conscious, holding the bag in front and pulling in the shoulders to look shorter.

qa.q: Why might volleyball practice help Tanvir?
qa.a: Enjoying movement where height is useful could help Tanvir feel at home in a changing body instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How does Yamini seem to see Tanvir's slouching?
qa.a: She recognises it from her own school years and responds with kind reassurance and an invitation rather than teasing.

grounding: Shows a teenager awkward about a growing body slumping and hiding behind a bag, and kind reassurance plus enjoyable movement offering a way to feel at home.
